requirements.evidence: All task and contract items are present: `app/Models/Entity.php:14-51` (fillable name/slug, SoftDeletes, slug route key, memberships/users/owner relations), `app/Models/EntityMembership.php:24-72` (UserRole cast, owner/admin/employee scopes, entity/user relations), `database/migrations/2026_10_29_062055_create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-28` (cascade FKs, role default, stored generated `owner_seq` plus the two named unique indexes), `app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:9-44` and `app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:10-44` (required abilities), `app/Http/Middleware/EnsureCurrentEntity.php:25-57` (session tenant, 403, zero/one/many empty-session rules), `app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:23-74` (validated name, owner creation through an action, collision retry, session, redirect, title), `app/Http/Controllers/HomeController.php:15-28` and `app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:14-34` (/home dispatch, pick, audit, switcher), `routes/web.php:22-31`, `resources/views/entity/switcher.blade.php:1-20`, `lang/pt_BR/ui.php:45-49` and `lang/en/ui.php:45-49`. Edge cases such as reserved `switcher` slug, stale session, soft-deleted slugs and the >1 navbar link are handled (`app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:57-74`, `app/Http/Middleware/EnsureCurrentEntity.php:38-40`, `resources/views/layouts/default-page.blade.php:14-16`).

conventions.evidence: Follows the project patterns: `#[Validate]` plus `$this->validate()` in `app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:23-31`; the domain write is an action authorizing internally (`app/Actions/CreateEntity.php:19-37`); authorization goes through policies in `app/Policies/*`; migrations are generated-style with reversible `down()` (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_062054_create_entities_table.php:1-32`, `..._062055_create_entity_memberships_table.php:1-39`); `#[Fillable]` is deliberate (`app/Models/Entity.php:14`, `app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13`); UI uses the existing layout and form components; Pest tests follow the suite. Docs are updated (`docs/database-schema.md`, `docs/business-rules.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/ops/logging.md`). The deviation is the duplicated CHANGELOG entry under the released `[0.0.0]` section (`CHANGELOG.md:40`).

security.evidence: Server-side authorization is applied everywhere it is needed: onboarding authorizes `create` before validating/persisting (`app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:28-30`) and the action authorizes again (`app/Actions/CreateEntity.php:21`); the dashboard authorizes `view` in `mount` and stores a `#[Locked]` model (`app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:14-22`); `pick` authorizes `view` before touching the session (`app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:22-34`); the middleware aborts 403 on a foreign session entity (`app/Http/Middleware/EnsureCurrentEntity.php:25-40`). Output is escaped with `{{ }}` (`resources/views/entity/switcher.blade.php:10-17`, `resources/views/livewire/entity/dashboard.blade.php:2`), fillable lists are minimal, no secrets are exposed, the custom middleware is persisted for Livewire updates (`app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:42-44`), and the tamper/unauthorized paths are covered. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: Six new Pest files cover the change: schema/constraints and cascades (`tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:13-121`), policies by role and cross-entity denial (`tests/Feature/EntityPoliciesTest.php:26-94`), onboarding happy path, validation, slug collisions, soft-deleted slugs, retry exhaustion, owner tampering and guest denial (`tests/Feature/OnboardingTest.php:20-175`), switcher/navbar/auth (`tests/Feature/EntitySwitcherTest.php:15-80`), dashboard 403, soft-deleted route, locked-property tamper and auth (`tests/Feature/EntityDashboardTest.php:15-86`), and /home plus the middleware's 403 and empty-session paths (`tests/Feature/TenantSessionTest.php:30-139`). The tests exercise failure and authorization paths, not only happy paths.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean and reused: the existing action/policy/layout/form-component patterns are used (`app/Actions/CreateEntity.php:19-37`, `app/Tenant/TenantContext.php:1-35`, `resources/views/entity/switcher.blade.php:1-20`) rather than introducing a service/repository layer. The one small duplication is the same `limit(2)` and 0/1/many dispatch in `app/Http/Controllers/HomeController.php:15-28` and `app/Http/Middleware/EnsureCurrentEntity.php:42-56`, which a tiny shared resolver could unify.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names and helpful docblocks (`EnsureCurrentEntity::handle`, `CreateEntity::uniqueSlug`, the policies), explanatory comments for the race and stale-session cases (`app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:34-36`, `app/Http/Middleware/EnsureCurrentEntity.php:38-39`), consistent sibling style, and no debug output or dead branches. Tests are named as behavior descriptions and are easy to follow.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: models/factories/migrations/policies, the tenant context/middleware and alias, the onboarding/switcher/dashboard routes, controllers, views, lang files and the required docs. There are no members/settings pages, no Accept-Language middleware, no Alpine navbar redesign and no card-layout centering changes. The reserved `switcher` slug is a small guard that keeps the new `/e/switcher` route reachable, not an unrelated feature.

issues.explanation: The same 'Entities and tenant session' bullet is added under both `[Unreleased]` and the already-released `[0.0.0] - 2026-07-07` section; the released section should not receive an unreleased feature entry, so the duplicate should be removed to keep the changelog accurate.
Both entry points re-implement the same `limit(2)` and zero/one/many membership dispatch; a small shared resolver would keep the two behaviors from drifting if the session rule changes.

review.summary: This change implements the full entity data model and policies, the tenant session and `current_entity` middleware, onboarding, switcher, dashboard, navbar entry, i18n and the required docs, with a strong Pest suite covering the failure and authorization paths. It meets the task and is secure; the only reasons for not approving as-is are a duplicated CHANGELOG entry under the released section and a small duplication of the zero/one/many dispatch logic.
